races.name: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai Apprentice Handicap Stakes (Whips To Be Carried But Not Used - A Racing Excellence Series)

runners_data.name: City Of God
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in this field and therefore likely to lead unchallenged; has a decent record at 8f on Standard but has not won on similar soft ground in a small sample, and the 21-day break is no concern — James Glennon's 5lb claim adds a further tactical plus from the front.

runners_data.name: Prince Rasam
runners_data.note: Returned to form with a close second over 10f on soft last time (99 days ago), suggesting he retains ability; hold-up by nature but the field dynamics may see him racing closer than usual, and Good To Soft conditions directly suit his profile.

runners_data.name: A La Noche
runners_data.note: Decent soft-ground bumper in recent form figures; a true hold-up horse by inclination who will find himself further forward than ideal given how many closers populate this field, and Oliver Hoodless takes the 5lb claim with a modest trainer strike rate to note.

runners_data.name: Thiscouldbefun
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip (8f, Good) and has placed twice at the distance; consistent prominent racer who should secure a natural berth tracking City Of God, making this race shape among the better setups she will face — Isobelle Chalmers keeps the ride.

runners_data.name: Special Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: Struggling for form on Good and faster ground through a long losing sequence; a natural hold-up horse who by necessity is mapped further forward than suits, and the trainer pairing carries a modest 14-day strike rate with Joe Bradnam in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Decalogue
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Jamie Osborne's yard (2 winners from 15 in 14 days) who placed third on Good over this trip — the most obvious "out of nowhere" live outsider given age allowance and trainer form; naturally holds up, which is genuinely his style and he gets the position more naturally than the redistributed rivals.

runners_data.name: Virtue Patience
runners_data.note: Placed at 8f on Standard and goes with headgear; a true hold-up mare who will be pushed forward of her comfort zone in this pace shape, and the 94-day absence after a modest recent run means fitness must be assumed rather than guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Musashi
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish flag noted — a genuine concern over a flat Salisbury mile where you cannot hide late weakness; held up by inclination, mapped mid-pack here, and 108 days off a race that ended in a 0 means significant fitness question surrounds this three-year-old despite the David Evans stable returning 2/18 in the 14-day window.

races.paceDynamic: City Of God is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to control the tempo from the front at whatever pace suits, making this a truly uncontested lead scenario on Good To Soft ground at Salisbury's flat mile. Thiscouldbefun and Prince Rasam are the next most prominent types, likely to track in second and third, while the bulk of the field — Decalogue, Musashi, Special Ghaiyyath, A La Noche and Virtue Patience — will be forced into a midfield or hold-up berth whether that suits them or not. On soft-ish ground over a flat mile with one horse dictating a measured, uncontested gallop, the race shape strongly favours those who can sit close to the pace and quicken from a handy position — prominent and stalking profiles — rather than those relying on a strong late surge from deep. This field holds considerably more hold-up types than the track position can accommodate; City Of God and Thiscouldbefun are best-placed to actually secure their natural roles, while A La Noche, Musashi, Special Ghaiyyath and Virtue Patience are genuine hold-up horses who will find themselves operating forward of their comfort zone.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: City Of God Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If City Of God rolls straight to the front and sets a controlled, honest gallop that suits soft ground without burning out.
scenarios.body: City Of God has a clear lead, uses the uncontested pace to preserve energy through the flat Salisbury mile, and the race becomes a test of who can sustain momentum into the final two furlongs rather than a sprint finish; prominent types that track close enough are best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If City Of God sets a strong enough pace to soften up the field and a close-tracking prominent type times their run to hit the front inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A stalker sitting second or third is ideally insulated from early effort and arrives with a full tank as the pace-setter tires on the soft ground; this rewards a horse that has held a clean position throughout the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If City Of God's lead is unexpectedly modest early, allowing the field to bunch and generating genuine late pace that plays into the hands of a hold-up type.
scenarios.body: A closer who has been dropped out conserves maximum energy through the bunched mid-race, and the flat Salisbury straight gives sufficient room to pick off tiring rivals; however, most redistributed hold-up runners are likely to be stationed mid-pack rather than deep, limiting true late-run benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse And Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If City Of God sets a breakneck early pace and capitulates, leaving the field in disarray with no horse having conserved energy properly.
scenarios.body: An open scramble develops in the final quarter-mile on testing ground with multiple front-running types having used up their reserves; any horse that happened to switch off unusually early and avoided the carnage could sneak through.

watchPoints.text: City Of God — if James Glennon allows her to drift too wide coming out of the stalls or is bustled for position early, the only front-runner in the race loses her key tactical advantage immediately.

Musashi — the "fades in finish" flag combined with 108 days off creates a live DNF or tailed-off risk that could disrupt the field's trailing order; Miss Amy Tucker (7lb claim) is an inexperienced rider to manage the situation.

Prince Rasam — returning after 99 days for Gary & Josh Moore; watch closely in the paddock and at the start for any sign of freshness or reluctance, as a fit-or-not question hangs over him despite promising recent form.

Thiscouldbefun — ran just 13 days ago, so monitor for any dullness in the preliminaries; if she shows her usual early keenness she is ideally placed to track City Of God throughout, but a flat show here is a significant tell against.

Decalogue and Virtue Patience — both hold-up types who will be tracking somewhere mid-pack in a field of closers; if the pace is genuinely slow and the field concertinas at halfway, any late burst from these two becomes far more potent than the race map alone suggests.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands A, B, C And D) (Div I) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands A, B, C And D) (Div II) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
British EBF Quidhampton Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
IRE-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish Dick Poole Fillies' Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Acclamation Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly whose one win came on Fibresand at 6f; all turf form on good ground gives a slight query over today's soft, and coming from off a 20-day break she needs a strong pace to deliver her late run from the rear.

runners_data.name: Dark Issue
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won last time at 6f on good and has placed twice at the same trip; Pat Dobbs keeps it simple, and with soft-ground form within the record the main concern is the 40-day layoff, though Richard Hannon's yard is capable of producing fresh winners.

runners_data.name: Elevating
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good and showed pace at 2f shorter than today's 6f; naturally wants to race up with the pace but the volume of prominent types means she is likely to be shuffled back into a midfield role that is not her preference, tempering confidence in her chance.

runners_data.name: Fillipas
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's filly has won at 6f on good and placed at 5f, but today she faces a similar problem to stablemate Lola De Valence — her front-running instincts will be compromised by the pace map, and racing off her natural rhythm from further back than ideal is a genuine handicap on soft ground.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Sky
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-running filly with five runs including a third at this trip on good; Silvestre De Sousa's positive booking adds interest, but her form string of 35364 suggests she finds one or two too good on the day, and she needs to step up in a stronger Grade 3 field.

runners_data.name: Impulsive Spirit
runners_data.note: Unbeaten juvenile with an eye-catching OR of 120, the highest in the field by some margin; she holds just one run on good ground over 5f, so the step to 6f on soft and Group 3 opposition are both unknowns Rob Hornby must navigate — the talent is clearly there but the risk is real.

runners_data.name: Lola De Valence
runners_data.note: Won her debut at 6f on good and placed at the same trip; a front-running type by nature who will likely find herself shuffled back into midfield territory because of the busy pace map, which blunts her effectiveness and suits her less than a small, clear-run race would.

runners_data.name: Love Is
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly by inclination with one win at 6f on good and a placed effort on soft; the 41-day break is the longest in the field, and her soft-going record (1 win, 1 place from 4 runs on similar) is the most relevant positive, but the redistribution note means she could race closer than her deepest form suggests.

runners_data.name: Miss Kodi
runners_data.note: Two wins from three starts, both at 6f on soft — the standout soft-ground profile in this field; Rossa Ryan is a reliable rider at this level, and Clive Cox places horses well, making her one of the most interesting prominent-type challengers in the race purely on applicable form.

runners_data.name: Miss Lizzy
runners_data.note: Six-race juvenile who won over 6f at Southwell (standard); all turf starts have been at 5f, so today's 6f on soft is unproven territory, and Paddy Bradley's booking on a 36-day break for a smaller yard is not a confidence booster in a Group 3.

runners_data.name: Nuit d'Eclair
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, which means she dictates pace without a rival to her flank on soft ground; Kevin Philippart De Foy's operation is in 14-day form (5/20), David Egan rides, and her sole win came at 6f on good — she trades on controlling tactics more than pure ability, but that advantage is real in this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Nuit d'Eclair is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, will be allowed to dictate from the front at a pace she controls on soft ground over 6f at Salisbury — a shape that is likely to be steady early and test stamina rather than pure speed in the closing stages. Prominent types Dark Issue, Harlequin Sky and Miss Kodi will sit just off her heels, while Elevating, Lola De Valence and Fillipas — all natural pace-presser types — are unlikely to secure their preferred positions given the volume of similar styles in this field, and will be shuffled back into midfield roles that do not suit them. The hold-up horses Acclamation Star, Miss Lizzy, Love Is and Impulsive Spirit begin from the rear and must hope the front sets a strong enough gallop to bring them into play late. This shape strongly favours the horse who travels prominently just behind the leader and has the class and stamina to overhaul Nuit d'Eclair in the final furlong — a prominent-to-pressing profile benefits most, particularly any runner proven on soft ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nuit d'Eclair Controls, Presser Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Nuit d'Eclair leads unchallenged and a close-tracking prominent horse collars her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Nuit d'Eclair sets a controlled, sustainable gallop that suits her own stamina but leaves the door open for a well-placed chaser who travels smoothly on her heels; soft ground rewards those pressing from second or third rather than those coming from deep. Dark Issue and Miss Kodi, both proven on soft and prominent by nature, are best positioned to deliver the decisive challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Nuit d'Eclair's controlled pace proves slow enough that the field never accelerates quickly enough to catch her.
scenarios.body: On soft ground at Salisbury the emphasis on stamina can reward a front-runner who dictates a modest tempo and never faces a serious injection of pace from behind; with the hold-up horses coming from too far back, Nuit d'Eclair could find enough reserves to hold them all off. Her recent course form and trainer's strong 14-day record support the view she is fit enough to front-run to victory.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Comes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is stronger than expected and the field strings out, bringing the closers into play in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Impulsive Spirit, unbeaten and lightly raced, carries a notably high OR of 120 for this grade and if Rob Hornby times the run perfectly from the rear she could have the raw ability to swamp the field late; Acclamation Star has shown a finishing kick on good ground before and might find soft ground limiting, but represents a viable each-way closer if the pace genuinely injures the front rank.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Crowded Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the squeeze of redistributed prominent types bunches the midfield, causing traffic and interference in the straight.
scenarios.body: Elevating, Lola De Valence and Fillipas, all pushed back from their natural prominent positions, create a congested mid-division that disrupts those trying to make progress from behind; in this scenario the only beneficiaries are those who had the clearest passage — likely Nuit d'Eclair on the front end or Dark Issue who races high and wide enough to avoid the scrimmage.

watchPoints.text: Impulsive Spirit's OR of 120 is a significant outlier in this field — if Rob Hornby delivers her with a clean run from the rear she has the raw rating to win regardless of race shape; watch how easily she travels through the ground from the half-mile marker.
Miss Kodi's two wins on soft at exactly this trip make her the standout on applicable going conditions — if she tracks Nuit d'Eclair in second or third early, a sustained challenge is very likely.

Elevating, Lola De Valence and Fillipas are all natural pace-presser types crowded into a midfield role they did not choose — monitor the first two furlongs for jostling and potential interference as these three try to find a rhythm outside their preferred style.

Love Is has the longest gap since her last run (41 days) in a field of mostly lightly-raced two-year-olds; Oisin Murphy's booking is a positive but fitness is not guaranteed, and if she needs the run her hold-up style offers no insurance early.

The going report consistently shows Good to Soft across every race at Salisbury today — stamina-enhancing but not dramatically testing; horses proven on this exact ground (Miss Kodi, Love Is) hold a measurable edge over those with only good-ground form.

races.name: European Bloodstock News EBF 'Lochsong' Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Havana Pusey
runners_data.note: A hold-up filly who wants to arrive late, though her recent 7f form on good ground and sim-going record of 0W0P at 6f on soft raises questions; Oisin Murphy boosts the booking but the drop to 6f against quicker types is a concern.

runners_data.name: Betty Clover
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's mare has been running over 7-8f and now drops to 6f on going softer than her best efforts; Oliver Carmichael claims 7lb, which helps offset a modest form string, and she sits naturally at the back of the field where a clear run is never guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Zen Diva
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan partners a progressive 3yo for Ralph Beckett who has won three of her last four starts at 6f including on good and similar surfaces; her prominent style puts her in the ideal position to stalk the front-runners and pounce, and her sim-going return of 0W1P in just one run slightly understates her profile.

runners_data.name: Stimulative Trip
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who has struggled in similar going with a sim-going record of 0W0P, and whose recent form shows a 9th and 8th on soft; Silvestre De Sousa takes over but the trip is on the short side for a filly whose wins came over 7f.

runners_data.name: Miss Nightcap
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner wearing headgear who has won back-to-back and will push immediately for the lead with Rob Hornby; she sets the pace for the whole field and her chance hinges on whether she can dictate without Angel Shared taking the race to her from the outset.

runners_data.name: Albaydaa
runners_data.note: William Haggas's 3yo drops to 6f having won over 7f on good and placed twice on soft; Harry Davies rides and her prominent style fits this pace map well — she can sit just behind the lead battle and challenge when the front pair weaken.

runners_data.name: Cindy Lou Who
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's 4yo has previous course-winning form at 6f and holds her own on similar surfaces with a sim-going record of 2W2P; she sits prominently and William Carson can use that experience, though her recent form has gone cold with five consecutive unplaced runs.

runners_data.name: Fleetwater
runners_data.note: J S Moore's 4yo has a genuine hold-up profile and has placed twice at 6f on soft-ish ground, but in a field with this much pace she is unlikely to get the wide-open late run she needs — her redistribution to midfield means she races partially out of role, and the STYLE_FIT flag should temper expectations accordingly.

runners_data.name: Passing Thought
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3yo has won at 6f on soft (sim-going 1W1P) and sits in a prominent map position; Kieran Shoemark is an astute pilot and if she can replicate her 6f soft win she will be competitive, though two unplaced runs since that win are a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Angel Shared
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner in the field who will fight Miss Nightcap for the early lead; Dougie Costello will aim to use her age and experience to win the pace battle, but her sim-going record of 0W0P on soft and a drop back to a weaker rating suggest her best chance is if Miss Nightcap blinks.

runners_data.name: Lyra Lea
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's 3yo has placed three times at 7-8f on good-soft and is a true hold-up filly, though in this competitive sprint she has been mapped to midfield as there is no room for her to settle tamely at the rear; Lewis Edmunds will need to find a clear line of running, and her STYLE_FIT tag reflects the mismatch.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Nightcap and Angel Shared are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the gates on this 6f Salisbury straight track, creating a genuinely contested pace on ground reported as Good to Soft throughout the card. That dual-lead battle, even at an honest rather than suicidal gallop, will apply early pressure and likely compress the margins between early and late portions of the race — soft ground will further tax those who burn energy in the first two furlongs. This race shape favours prominent racers who can track just off the pace without expending energy in the lead battle, and then sustain their effort through the final two furlongs on softening ground — horses like Zen Diva and Albaydaa are ideally profiled to exploit this. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Fleetwater and Lyra Lea are genuine closers but have been redistributed into midfield, as they are unlikely to secure their natural wide-open late run in a field where traffic and pace shape will make a truly patient ride difficult.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Nightcap and Angel Shared lock horns for the lead and set a honest-to-strong early pace on soft ground, a prominent tracker arrives fresh to the weakening lead horses.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners soften each other on ground that punishes early exertion, leaving a horse settled just off the pace in the perfect position to pounce inside the final furlong; soft going rewards those who conserve energy through the first half.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lead Softens, Hold-Up Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go quick enough early that the closers, given a clear passage, can make up significant ground in the final furlong on the soft surface.
scenarios.body: The pace collapse in the final furlong would suit a genuine hold-up horse finishing fastest of all, with soft ground extending the race time and rewarding the deepest stayer; however this shape is partly discounted because Fleetwater and Lyra Lea are not guaranteed their ideal patient position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Shared or Miss Nightcap gets a clear break and the other fails to press hard enough, allowing one to control fractions and ration their effort.
scenarios.body: A lone leader on soft ground at 6f can set a comfortable tempo, and a hold on the rail at Salisbury is a genuine tactical advantage; Miss Nightcap's recent back-to-back wins and hg entry make her the likelier beneficiary if this soft lead materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Late Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position causes the pace to be uneven or collapse mid-race, creating a scramble in the closing stages that opens the door for unexposed or big-priced runners.
scenarios.body: A confused gallop on soft ground could play tricks on race-shape predictions and bring an out-of-form or underrated runner into play; with 11 runners and genuine pace conflict, positional trouble is a realistic if unlikely disruptor.

watchPoints.text: Miss Nightcap and Angel Shared — watch the first furlong closely; if both go flat out for the lead the pace could be genuinely taxing on soft ground, accelerating the collapse of front-runners turning for home.

Fleetwater and Lyra Lea — both are natural closers mapped out of their preferred position; if traffic develops in the mid-to-rear section of this 11-runner field their chance could be compromised before the race even develops.

Zen Diva — her three recent wins at 6f make her the standout prominent type on form, but Rossa Ryan must ensure she does not get caught in the early pace battle; if she covers up smoothly she is the horse to beat on scenario probability.

Going: the card has been consistently reported as Good to Soft all afternoon despite the official Soft designation for this race — if the ground is faster than expected, Miss Nightcap's front-running profile becomes considerably more potent.
Passing Thought — has won at 6f on soft before (form: 1/6f/SOF in hist) and could be underestimated if her recent disappointing runs are excused by unsuitably long trips.

races.name: Madar Corporation Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Boyfriend
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-maker here; Pat Dobbs takes the mount and he goes well fresh (LR 33d), but his best form is over 9f-10f and the soft ground at 8f uncontested may see him idle and get caught; STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence despite the prime tactical position.

runners_data.name: One Smack Mac
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has struggled at 7f-8f in good ground and posted a string of disappointing finishes; William Carver's claim helps at the weights but there is very little in his recent record to suggest he fires on this going or trip.

runners_data.name: Principality
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's 4yo ran just four days ago yet handles soft well — 1W2P in similar going — and Kaiya Fraser claims 3lbs; the horse has form both sides of the going spectrum at 8f, making him one of the most versatile profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Skipper
runners_data.note: Hamad Al Jehani's yard has been in good form (T14: 3/17) and Kieran Shoemark is a strong booking; blinkers fitted and one win in good-to-soft on record at this trip, but the soft-ground figures are thin — maps to a prominent position he can likely hold.

runners_data.name: Point Of Contact
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Balding and the horse is a proven winner at 9f in good going; though a natural prominent racer, the congested pace map means he may find himself shuffled further back than ideal, blunting his usual forward-tracking advantage.

runners_data.name: Looka
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa partners Marco Botti's 3yo who wears no headgear and drops back from 8f-10f company; best form at 7f on standard tracks, and the soft ground at a mile represents a question his limited form sample cannot fully answer yet.

runners_data.name: Colourband
runners_data.note: The Crisford 3yo arrives on the back of a recent win, races prominently by inclination, and maps into a good stalking berth; hood fitted, and soft-ground form (4/10f/SOF) shows he handles cut, though he steps back from 10f, which may actually suit on this going.

runners_data.name: Time Loop
runners_data.note: William Haggas's 5yo is a genuine prominent runner by nature but is squeezed into a midfield slot by the pace map — racing out of role is a real concern; 75 days off the track adds uncertainty, and his best form was over 10f-12f on standard surfaces, making this trip short.

runners_data.name: Shipbourne
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 3yo has a smart profile — wins at 6f and 7f on soft and good — and Colin Keane is a top rider; he has been absent 56 days and his lone 1m run ended in a distant 13th, so the step up in trip carries genuine uncertainty despite the class angle.

runners_data.name: Zoffandia
runners_data.note: Keiran Burke's 5yo is a true hold-up horse nudged into a midfield slot for mapping purposes; visor and tongue-tie fitted, 83 days off the track, and a record showing just one win from 15 runs on similar going — this is a horse who needs everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Electric Dreams
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's 3yo is a natural hold-up type who won impressively on good at 8f but has since disappointed; placed in midfield by redistribution rather than natural inclination, and with only four career runs his profile is too lightly raced to inspire great confidence at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Boyfriend is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with a field of 11 on soft ground over Salisbury's flat mile, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable but uncontested tempo — nobody is going to pressurise him off a fast early pace in these conditions. Skipper and Colourband are the natural prominent horses most likely to actually secure positions just behind him, while Point Of Contact and Time Loop are genuine front-runners by inclination but are mapped into midfield because there are more prominent types in this field than positions available — they will likely be shuffled back against their nature. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate, meaning Point Of Contact and Time Loop are the horses most at risk of racing in an uncongenial position, with Boyfriend and Skipper best placed to control the tempo. A soft-ground mile at Salisbury run at a steady, uncontested pace strongly favours horses who can sit prominently in the first two or three and quicken into the straight without having ground to make up — patient hold-up types who need genuine pace to chase will find it harder to generate momentum from the back on this ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Boyfriend Controls; Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Boyfriend dictates a steady gallop and the prominent holders track him into the straight.
scenarios.body: Boyfriend sets a sustainable tempo on soft ground, leaving Skipper and Colourband in ideal tracking positions to challenge turning in; the steady pace suits those with a quick turn of foot over the last two furlongs rather than those needing a searching gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses; Closers Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If Boyfriend's gallop is genuinely slow and hold-up horses finish fastest of all.
scenarios.body: A crawl through the early stages creates a sprint finish over the last two furlongs, which in theory opens the door for Principality and Looka from behind; however, several of the nominal hold-up types here are redistributed prominent runners, so their ability to produce a true closer's burst is questionable.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Pressured; Prominent Tires
scenarios.trigger: If Point Of Contact or Time Loop press forward against their mapped position and force a stronger tempo.
scenarios.body: A more contested gallop on soft ground stretches the field and sees the front two tire in the final furlong, handing the advantage to a well-rated hold-up horse who travels smoothly into the gaps.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the ground plays significantly slower than Good To Soft and stamina becomes the dominant factor.
scenarios.body: The mile becomes a genuine test of endurance in the final stages and horses with proven soft-ground form at this trip come to the fore; Principality's repeated placed efforts on soft and Shipbourne's prior wins on testing ground give them the profile edge.

watchPoints.text: Colourband — if he secures a prominent position tracking Boyfriend through the first half, his recent form, soft-ground evidence and Rossa Ryan's horsemanship make him the most dangerous horse to come from the chasing pack.

Principality — ran four days ago yet holds genuine soft-ground form and Kaiya Fraser's 3lb claim is meaningful at these weights; watch whether he travels smoothly in the hold-up group because he could arrive late with a real run.

Point Of Contact — if Oisin Murphy decides to push forward against the tide and force a prominent position, it could create a more pressured pace than Boyfriend wants and disturb the entire race shape.

Time Loop — 75 days off the track for Haggas is worth monitoring in the betting ring; if well-supported despite the lay-off, he may be working at home and a forward move from his natural style could compress the pace.

Shipbourne — Colin Keane's tactical intelligence is worth watching early; if he sends Shipbourne forward to claim a position rather than settling mid-to-rear, it signals the camp expects the mile trip to be within range and changes the competitive picture.

races.name: Lester Aldridge Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Redbud Sixteen
runners_data.note: Recent 1m2f winner on Good ground and has form figures of 1-1 over this trip; the big concern is a 62-day absence and the step up to soft, but confirmed lead style means it will at least shape the race from the front.

runners_data.name: Zgharta
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy retains the ride for the powerful Andrew Balding yard which fires at 19% over 14 days; hold-up style suits the anticipated strong pace, and three runs on soft or similar show reasonable tolerance for this ground, though the horse has yet to win at this trip.

runners_data.name: Aleatrix
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old has won on her only two starts at 1m2f on Good and is a confirmed front-runner who will go head-to-head with Redbud Sixteen; the soft ground is an unknown given her limited profile, but Rossa Ryan is a shrewd judge at this venue.

runners_data.name: Lucky Camino
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer — five starts, four placed finishes — who races prominently and was second at 1m on Soft last time; the step to 1m2f looks a logical move for Hugo Palmer's stable, and Harry Davies keeps the ride after guiding it to a course win on Good.

runners_data.name: Chapter
runners_data.note: Won over 1m2f on Good and carries a hood today for Charles Hills; a genuine hold-up type whose best chance arrives if the pace duel delivers a truly honest gallop, and Rob Hornby's patient style suits this race shape well.

runners_data.name: Leonardo Blu
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 1m on Good and finished second over the same trip; stepping up to 1m2f for the first time, which is the key question, but Tom Clover's yard is in fair 14-day form and David Egan's experience at getting horses into position is an asset.

runners_data.name: Kamaway
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's gelding has winning form on Good over 1m and is a true hold-up horse by nature, though congestion at the rear of this field means it is likely to race in a more midfield position than suits it best; the reduced STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) tempers confidence, and the OR drop to 72 hints at a horse seeking its level.

races.paceDynamic: Redbud Sixteen and Aleatrix are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over Salisbury's 1m2f trip on Good to Soft ground, creating a genuinely contested early pace rather than a procession. That duel is likely to produce an honest, even relentless gallop through the first half of the race, with neither likely to concede ground cheaply given both have recent winning form in front. The sustained pace on soft ground over a staying trip tilts the balance firmly towards hold-up horses and genuine closers who can travel within themselves before producing a measured late run — Zgharta, Chapter, and Kamaway all profile as potential beneficiaries of this shape. Kamaway is a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more genuine rear-pacers than the visual positions can accommodate; Redbud Sixteen and Aleatrix are best placed to actually secure the front positions they are drawn for.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Redbud Sixteen and Aleatrix battle for the lead and the honest gallop drains both before the home straight.
scenarios.body: The sustained early duel on soft ground burns through the pace setters, leaving the track open for horses who have been covered up and travelling smoothly; the 1m2f trip on this going rewards stamina and a patient ride over raw speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of Aleatrix or Redbud Sixteen blinks and allows the other to stride clear uncontested at a controlled pace.
scenarios.body: The surviving leader settles into a rhythm and saves enough for a strong finish, dictating terms with enough cover left to repel late challenges; Aleatrix's more recent two-run form profile and slightly higher OR makes her the more likely candidate to thrive in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Gaps The Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel blows up early enough that a prominent mid-group horse drafts through on the inner before the closers can organise.
scenarios.body: Lucky Camino and Leonardo Blu, both sitting just off the pace, are ideally placed to exploit any collapse of the lead pair and reach the line before the hold-up horses can quicken through; their proximity to the action and consistent placed form makes them the main dangers in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Reach Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves steadier than expected despite two front-runners and soft ground blunts the finishing kick of hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A moderate tempo would insulate the leaders from being run down by Zgharat and Chapter, who need a strong gallop to make up ground on this going; this is the least likely shape given the structural pressure from two genuine pace-setters.

watchPoints.text: Redbud Sixteen and Aleatrix — watch whether either jockey blinks at the break; if one tries to go easy on the other the pace dissolves and the whole dynamic shifts away from closers.

Zgharat — Oisin Murphy will be tracking the pace duel from behind but needs the gallop to remain honest all the way to the home turn on Salisbury's flat track; if the tempo drops the 34-day break and step up in trip become more costly.
Lucky Camino — watch its position at the halfway point; if it drifts wider than ideal around the home bend, the prominent runner's advantage narrows sharply and the hold-up horses can close the gap.

Kamaway — genuine hold-up horse likely to race further forward than ideal given the crowded rear of the field; watch whether Rhys Clutterbuck can find a clear run in the straight or finds itself boxed in as the pace pair tire.
Chapter — headgear (hood) first time for Charles Hills; watch early behaviour and whether the hood sharpens its early action enough to improve its tactical position at the start.
